newsitem.title: USA: TENNNIS-BJORKMAN WINS INDIANAPOLIS MEN'S TOURNAMENT.
newsitem.headline: TENNNIS-BJORKMAN WINS INDIANAPOLIS MEN'S TOURNAMENT.

text.p: Jonas Bjorkman kept his
concentration during a 30-minute rain delay Sunday and beat
fifth-seeded Spaniard Carlos Moya 6-3 7-6 (7-3) to win the $1
million RCA Championships, his second title of the year.
The 25-year-old Swede, seeded ninth, will move into a
career-high ranking in the top 20 of the ATP Tour Monday as a
result of his effort in a final that was briely halted after
the third game of the second set by light rain.
"I got off to a great start," said Bjorkman, currently
23rd in the world. "I had a lot of power on my strokes and
played great from the baseline. I was able to move Carlos
around today instead of him moving me. I'm glad it was over in
two sets."
The win was revenge for the Swede after Moya beat him in
five sets at the Australian Open in January.
The title gives Davis Cup semifinalist Sweden seven for
the year on the ATP Tour and boosts Scandinavian hopes for a
good performance at the U.S. Open, starting a week from
Monday.
Bjorkman broke twice in the first set and came back from a
break down in the second with a break-back in the fourth game
after the rain interruption. The contest went to a tiebreaker,
which the Swede won on his first of three match points.
"I didn't make too many mistakes today, that was the
difference," said Bjorkman. "Last time, I tried to overpower
him by hitting too many tough shots.
"Today I was waiting and took the chance when I got a
short ball and was aggressive on them.
Bjorkman added the title to the first of his career, won
in Auckland in Janaury. He was beaten by Australian Jason
Stoltenberg in the title match at Coral Springs, Florida, in
May.
"This title feels much better than the one I won in
Auckland," he said. "That was the week before the Australian
Open and not everyone was playing. Here, there was a top field
(headed by Pete Sampras).
"I was going to go out there and enjoy myself. I was also
hoping to win it, but I didn't put too much pressure on
myself, that was the key."
Moya was plagued by forehand errors, but added: "I'm glad
to have made the final, but I'm very disappointed to have
lost.
"I was patchy today. The rain delay was not great, but it
was the same for both of us."
